transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

My wife and adult son actually pushed me to come get evaluated today. They say I’ve been acting all over the place at work and at home, like I can’t control what I’m doing or keep it appropriate to what’s going on.
Have you ever had a similar period before when you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or acted this way? Or is this the first time it has ever happened?
No, I've never felt unusually energized or needed less sleep. This is definitely the first time I've ever experienced these kinds of disorganized thoughts and behaviors.

Before these disorganized thoughts and behaviors started, did you have any recent medical illness, head injury, seizure, or start/stop any medications, alcohol, or drugs? If so, what happened and when?
No, I haven't had any head injuries, seizures, or major medical illnesses before all of this started. I also haven't started or stopped any medications, and I don't use alcohol or recreational drugs.
How long have these disorganized thoughts and behaviors been going on, from when they first started until now? Have they lasted less than a month, or longer?

It has definitely been longer than a month. I first started gradually coming apart about a year ago when they rolled out a new inventory system at work, but the really jumbled thoughts and behaviors have been clearly off the rails for about the last six months.

Have you been hearing voices or felt that people are spying on you, plotting against you, or trying to harm you? Or has the main problem been confused thinking and behavior without those kinds of experiences?

No, I haven't heard any voices or felt like anyone is spying on or plotting against me. The main problem is definitely just my confused thinking and these strange behaviors, like getting completely lost in patterns or pacing and flapping my hands without being able to stop.

final_diagnosis.reason: Presentation is most consistent with disorganized schizophrenia: prominent disorganized thinking and behavior, including bizarre/stereotyped motor behavior, lasting well over 1 month and clearly active for about 6 months, without evidence of substance/medical causation, mania, or prominent hallucinations/persecutory delusions. The gradual deterioration and functional disruption support a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder, specifically the disorganized subtype code provided.
